mia: Ran a cross-topology perf pass today (8x A100 split into 2 NVLink domains vs 8x across PCIe + EFA). Seeing a weird pattern: all-reduce pauses when TP>1 on EFA runs, KV cache misses spike around rpc boundaries, and the runtime is choosing an unfused fp16 kernel at seq_len=2048 which is ~12% slower overall. Trace attached in thread (large).

sam: can you paste the top-level perf markers? like compute/comm overlap, barrier times?

mia: pasted snippets below. TL;DR: compute blocks ~40ms, all-reduce windows show 15-25ms gaps with no compute overlapped. KV cache hit rate drops from 92% -> 68% when requests route across hosts.

mia: ```
# simplified timeline (ms)
0-120 compute (shard 0)
120-140 allreduce (small)
140-200 compute
200-225 allreduce (large)  <-- idle spikes here on EFA runs
225-320 compute
```

mia: NCCL logs show multiple rendezvous retries on EFA for ranks that are not NVLink connected.

priya: interesting — sounds like topology-aware grouping might help. we should prefer intra-node NVLink groups for tensor parallel placements, then route cross-node via async allreduce. also the KV cache invalidation on RPC boundaries is bad: we only serialize prefix KV when we checkpoint, not on RPC shuffle.

jorge: +1 on grouping. also odd that kernel selector picks unfused path at 2k seq; is selector using per-device microbenchmarks or a global profile?

mia: selector currently uses per-GPU microbench but aggregated by rank type; if a rank sees high comm stall it biases toward lower-memory but slower kernels (hence the unfused path). we may be triggering a bad feedback loop.

nate: Do we have numeric delta for latency/throughput between fabrics? even coarse numbers help.

mia: quick numbers from the synthetic run (same batch mix, same model):
- NVLink (all ranks intra-host groups): throughput = 14k tokens/s, p95 token latency = 110ms
- PCIe+EFA (naive placement): throughput = 9.8k tokens/s, p95 = 155ms
- Observed p99 tails are dominated by allreduce stalls and RPC rehydration of KV cache.

priya: Possible mitigation list:
- topology-aware TP placement (prefer NVLink peers)
- async / pipelined allreduce for gradients/KV to overlap more with compute
- KV prefix sticky routing: keep cache-affine requests pinned to same host when possible
- kernel-selector guard to avoid switching to unfused path until sustained perf drop > X iterations

sam: on KV routing: we should be careful — pinning increases hot-spot risk. maybe soft-affinity with weighted routing: prefer local host but fallback based on capacity.

mia: agree. I prototyped a soft-affinity scheduler: pref_count = local_capacity*0.75, then probabilistic spill. Early results: KV hit rate rises back to ~88% and throughput improves ~10% on mixed traffic.

jorge: For comm/compute overlap, can we do deferred allreduce + small window incremental reductions? i.e., split big allreduce into two async phases so the first chunk reduces smaller tensors asap and second finishes later. might help hide the 15-25ms stall.

mia: tried chunked allreduce in userland: reduced visible stall by ~8ms but increased CPU scheduling overhead. Need integrated runtime support.

nate: any repro script or job config I can run on perf infra? I'll try to reproduce on our PCIe+EFA cluster.

mia: pushed the perf harness to ci/perf/topo-kv-efa (job: perf-topo-kv-efa). quick run command: 
```
./tools/perf_runner --model gpt-small --tp 2 --pp 1 --batch 8 --seq 2048 --topology pci_efa --runs 50
```

infra-bot: CI job perf-topo-kv-efa triggered by mia in project perf/topo-kv-efa (build 3921).

priya: action items:
- mia: open PR for soft-affinity KV routing + perf tests (short-lived experimental flag)
- jorge: draft runtime patch for chunked async allreduce (prototype)
- sam: evaluate kernel-selector hysteresis threshold and add guard
- nate: repro on perf infra and capture pprof + NCCL logs

mia: noted. I'll attach perf tarball and a short guide in the PR. thanks all. :thumbsup:

sam: one more ask — can we add a topology map export to the console (NVLink groups + host adjacency) so runtime decisions are visible for tenants? would help debugging customer cases.

priya: yes please; that mapping should be read-only by default but downloadable for enterprise customers.

mia: marking this thread as summary for the perf ticket: INF-4723. I'll link the PR and perf artifacts there.
